### __partiesAL__:  Legislative Parties of the Americas Since 1925


*Aníbal Pérez-Liñán, Nicolás Schmidt, Daniela Vairo*



<!-- badges: start -->
`r badger::badge_devel("Nicolas-Schmidt/partiesAL", "orange")`
[![Project Status: Active – The project has reached a stable, usable state and is being actively developed.](https://www.repostatus.org/badges/latest/active.svg)](https://www.repostatus.org/#active)

<!-- badges: end -->



## Description
The partiesAL package provides two interconnected datasets on legislative parties and political coalitions across 21 countries in the Americas, including 20 Latin American countries and the United States. The current version covers the period from 1925 to 2024, with ongoing updates to incorporate new legislative periods.

The first dataset, parties, contains annual information on political parties and their legislative representation, with the party (or party faction) as the unit of analysis. It includes data on legislative seats, party affiliations, presidential parties, and governing coalitions.

The second dataset, parties2, aggregates this information at the country-year level and provides additional indicators of party system characteristics, including the effective number of parties and the legislative strength of presidents and governing coalitions in both chambers of congress.

Users can access the data by installing the partiesAL R package using the instructions below. Alternatively, both datasets are available for direct download in CSV, XLSX, and Stata (DTA) formats, allowing their use across different statistical software environments.

Detailed definitions and coding procedures for all variables are provided in the accompanying codebook, available through the link below.

## `parties` and `parties2`

The structure of the databases is as follows

```{r}
str(partiesAL::parties)
```


```{r}
str(partiesAL::parties2)
```




## Installation

To install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
if (!require("remotes")) install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Nicolas-Schmidt/partiesAL")
```


## Example
```{r, echo=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

```

In the following example, the `parties` database is used to visualize the temporal evolution of the number of political parties in the congresses of each country.



```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 12}
library(partiesAL)

nparty <- 
    partiesAL::parties %>% 
    select(ccode, pty_code, year, legis) %>% 
    filter(legis %in% c(1,3)) %>% 
    distinct() %>%
    select(-pty_code, - legis) %>% 
    split(., .$ccode) %>% 
    lapply(., table) %>% 
    lapply(., as.data.frame) %>% 
    do.call('rbind', .) 


ggplot(nparty, aes(x = as.numeric(as.character(year)), y = Freq))+
    geom_bar(stat="identity", width = NULL, fill = "#279F00", color = "black") + 
    facet_wrap(~ccode, ncol = 3) + 
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "", y = "")


```
